why: A session starts from the handoff pack rather than from the PRD.
SEEN-104 wrote the pack; this is what makes reading it the default
instead of an instruction a session can skip.
The budget is a cap only if the session hears about it before it spends
the next turn. A warning after the fact is a report.
One matcher for both assistants: each matches on the tool names it has,
so the union names Edit, Write and MultiEdit on the Claude Code side and
apply_patch on the Codex side, with no per-client matcher to keep in step.
Ten seconds because this one runs in front of every edit.
Both, because both compact: codex-cli 0.156.1 carries a JSON Schema for
this event, so a Codex session that compacts can write its pack too, and
a session losing the pack is what this event exists to prevent. Both
triggers, because the automatic one is the one nobody chose and so the
one that loses the context.
Both, for the reason PreCompact is: the same schemas name this event, so
a Codex reviewer is held to the findings rule as well. Which agent
stopped is read from the payload rather than from a matcher, because the
matcher on this event is not documented as matching an agent name.
The self-check at the end of a turn, quick rather than whole: the sections
that read the journal and the generated copies, and none that walks
the tree.
